question: What are the three sentences of a LinkedIn cold outreach message?

●​ Alumni tool
         ○​ Navigating: Search school name in search bar > Click on school > Click on
            “Alumni” tab on home page
         ○​ Filtering: Search alumni by desired function (e.g. “product manager”, be sure to
            use quotes). You can continue to filter by company
         ○​ Connecting: If you find someone with whom you want to connect and message,

  ●​ Linkedin cold outreach message guidelines (Commonality, Curiosity, and Call-to-Action)
         ○​ Sentence #1: Prove you’re not a stranger, state what you have in common: “I’m a

         ○​ Sentence #2: State what you are looking for–learning, a referral, a job, etc: “I’m
            torn between a PM and consulting career path and would love to learn from your
            expertise.”
○​ Sentence #3: Take all the friction out of the process: “Any chance you have 10

●​ Linkedin recruiter gives people access to half a billion professionals globally. The tool is
     most geared towards 1) number of instances of key words (e.g. “brand marketing,”
     “product marketing,” etc.) 2) closeness of connection, and 3) photo
  ●​ Most important key word is the job title itself; most important placement: 1) Headline 2)
     Summary/About 3) Experience
         ○​ The algorithm places a high value on words in these three categories because
            they are the sections with the smallest character limit, placing greater value on
            the words within them
         ○​ Headline: “Aspiring Product Manager” or “Seeking Product Manager Roles”

answer:
The three sentences of a LinkedIn cold outreach message are:
1. Prove you’re not a stranger, state what you have in common: “I’m a current/alumni of (school), and I was thrilled to come across your profile” [S1].
2. State what you are looking for–learning, a referral, a job, etc: “I’m torn between a PM and consulting career path and would love to learn from your expertise” [S1].
3. Take all the friction out of the process: “Any chance you have 10 minutes for a quick Zoom chat?” [S1].
